After 15 years at the helm, today is officially the last day of Tim Cook as Apple CEO. In April this year, Apple announced that Cook would step down as CEO on 1 September, with John Ternus taking over.

Cook of course will not be leaving entirely — he will transition to the role of executive chairman of Apple's board of directors.

Tim Cook's final day as Apple CEO

Cook took over as Apple CEO in 2011, just two months after Steve Jobs' passing. Ternus joined Apple in 2001 as part of the product design team, and rose steadily through the ranks, formally being promoted to Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering in January 2021.

In a weekend report, Bloomberg reiterated that Cook, in his new role as executive chairman, will focus on handling Apple's relationships with US President Trump and the Chinese government.

Bloomberg noted that Ternus is expected to move into Cook's current office upon assuming the CEO role. The Information also reported that Cook's executive assistant will remain in post and continue to work for Ternus.

Reports indicate that Apple held a farewell dinner for Cook at Apple Park last week, during which Ternus, Laurene Powell Jobs, and other current and former Apple executives spent hours paying tribute to Cook. Cook's favourite band OneRepublic also performed at the event.

The leadership transition comes ahead of Apple's "Surprise and Shine" special event on Wednesday, 9 September. Cook will not be present at the event, which will be hosted by Ternus. Expectations are high that Apple will unveil a number of new products, including a foldable iPhone Ultra, the iPhone 18 Pro, and several new Apple Watch models.

In recent weeks, Apple has faced criticism for a string of announcements, including price hikes on most hardware products (excluding iPhones) as well as subscription services such as Apple TV, Apple Music and Apple One. This move effectively paves the way for Ternus to focus on what has been hailed as the most ambitious product cycle in Apple's history.

Are you excited about Ternus taking over as Apple CEO tomorrow? What changes would you like to see him make? How would you rate Cook's tenure? Let us know in the comments.
